- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Acoustic pianos are traditional instruments that use strings and a soundboard to produce sound, divided into grand and upright pianos.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Digital pianos replicate the sound and feel of acoustic pianos using digital technology and offer features like portability and lower maintenance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Hybrid pianos combine elements of both acoustic and digital pianos, providing an authentic feel along with digital convenience.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Player pianos are self-playing instruments that use a built-in system to play pre-recorded music, available in both acoustic and digital formats.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Specialty pianos cater to specific niches or offer unconventional playing experiences, such as toy pianos and prepared pianos.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Digital pianos can be an excellent alternative to acoustic pianos for beginners due to their affordability and built-in features.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Hybrid pianos provide the authentic feel and sound of an acoustic piano along with the convenience of a digital piano.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Player pianos use a built-in system to play pre-recorded music, with both acoustic and digital options available.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A prepared piano is altered by placing objects on or between the strings to create unusual sounds.
